authn.accountNoLongerSignedIn: That account is no longer signed in here. Choose it again to sign in, or choose another.
authn.accountNotRemembered: That account is not one this browser remembers.
authn.accountSessionEnded: That account's session has just ended. Choose it again to sign in, or choose another.
authn.accountStillSignedIn: That account is still signed in. Sign it out first; only a signed-out account can be forgotten.
authn.accountsChanged: The accounts in this browser changed in another tab. Choose again.
authn.accountsFull: This browser is already signed in to {count} accounts, the most it may hold. Sign out of one of them first.
authn.accountsUnread: This browser's accounts could not be read just now. Try again in a moment.
authn.authenticatorAppNotSetUp: The authenticator app could not be set up.
authn.authenticatorAppsOff: Authenticator apps cannot be set up in this realm.
authn.browserAnswerUnreadable: The browser returned something this server could not read.
authn.browserNoCeremonySignIn: Your browser did not run the ceremony. Signing in with a passkey needs JavaScript — a passkey is used by the browser and no form can do it. Allow scripts for this page, or type your username.
authn.browserNoCeremonyStep: Your browser did not run the ceremony. This step needs JavaScript — a passkey is used by the browser and no form can do it. Allow scripts for this page and try again.
authn.browserNoPasskey: Your browser did not use a passkey ({error}).
authn.certificateNotOffered: Signing in with a certificate is not offered for this sign-in.
authn.choosePasskeyFirst: Choose one of your passkeys first.
authn.chooseSecondFactorFirst: Choose a second factor to set up first.
authn.codeUncheckedTryAgain: That code could not be checked. Try again.
authn.codeUncheckedTryNext: That code could not be checked. Try the next one.
authn.enterUsername: Enter a username. It does not have to exist — it is the identity the issued tokens will describe.
authn.keyAloneAccountNeedsTwo: A second factor is required for this account, and a security key on its own is one factor. Sign in with your password; you will be asked for your second factor, or to set one up.
authn.keyAloneRealmNeedsTwo: A second factor is required in this realm, and a security key on its own is one factor. Sign in with your password; you will be asked for your second factor, or to set one up.
authn.linkNeedsPassword: Linking an account signs in with its password — and its second factor, where it has one — so a security key on its own is not offered here.
authn.newPasswordNotAccepted: The new password was not accepted.
authn.noClassicalPasskeyLeft: There is no classical passkey to upgrade any more.
authn.noPasskeyRegistered: There is no passkey registered for signing in to this account. Sign in with your password, then add a passkey at /portal/keys.
authn.passkeyAloneNotTwo: This request asked for a second factor, so a passkey on its own cannot answer it — one factor is one factor. Sign in with a password and the passkey together.
authn.passkeyBeforeUsernameless: This passkey was registered before passkeys could sign in without a username. Type your username to use it, or register it again at /portal/keys.
authn.passkeyCouldNotSignIn: That passkey could not sign you in.
authn.passkeyNameNotUsername: That is the name your password manager shows for a post-quantum passkey, not a username. Type your username without the part after the "+".
authn.passkeyNeededNoneHeld: This request needs a passkey, and this account holds none. Add one at /portal/keys and sign in again.
authn.passkeyNotUpgradable: The passkey could not be upgraded.
authn.passkeyRequestExpired: That passkey request has expired. Try again.
authn.passkeyUncheckedUnchanged: The passkey could not be checked. Your passkey is unchanged; try again.
authn.passkeysOffNoRegistration: Passkeys are switched off in this realm (webauthn.enabled), so a new one cannot be registered here. A passkey already registered goes on working.
authn.passwordNotFirstFactor: This realm does not accept a password as a first factor. Use one of the other ways of signing in below.
authn.passwordReserved: That password is reserved and is refused at every sign-in, so it cannot be yours.
authn.passwordsDiffer: The two passwords are not the same.
authn.postLoginNotSkippable: The time allowed for this has passed, so it cannot be skipped any more. Register the passkey to finish signing in.
authn.postQuantumOnlyStep: This step registers a post-quantum passkey only; a classical one cannot be made here.
authn.secondFactorAlreadySetUp: A second factor is already set up for this account. Start the request again from the application that sent you here and sign in with it.
authn.secondFactorCheckFailed: The second factor did not verify; this check failed: {checks}.
authn.secondFactorNoneForApplication: A second factor is required, and none that this application accepts can be set up here. Ask an administrator.
authn.secondFactorNoneInRealm: A second factor is required for this account and none can be set up here: authenticator apps and security keys are both switched off in this realm. Ask an administrator.
authn.secondFactorNotOptional: A second factor is required for this account; it cannot be ignored.
authn.secondFactorUnchecked: The second factor could not be checked: {detail}
authn.securityKeysOff: Security keys cannot be set up in this realm.
authn.setUpExpired: That set-up expired before it was confirmed. Start it again.
authn.stepEnded: This sign-in step has already ended. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
authn.stepExpired: This second-factor step has expired. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
authn.usernamelessOnly: This application signs in with a passkey and no username. Use Sign in with a passkey.
authn.webauthnError: {error} (WebAuthn reports one error for several situations, so this does not say which.)
consent.formExpired: This consent form has expired, or it has already been answered. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
consent.nobodySignedIn: Nobody is signed in here any more, so there is nobody to record an answer for. Start the request again from the application that sent you here.
consent.nobodySignedInAnswer: Nobody is signed in here any more, so this answer belongs to nobody. Nothing was recorded.
consent.nothingWaiting: There is no consent waiting under that id, or it has expired. Start the request again from the application that sent you here — nothing was issued and nothing was recorded.
consent.otherPerson: This consent was asked of "{asked}" and the session in this browser belongs to "{signedIn}". It is refused rather than recorded against whoever happens to be signed in, which is the one failure at this door that would write something untrue into the directory.
consent.otherPersonAnswer: This consent was asked of "{asked}" and this browser is signed in as "{signedIn}". Nothing was recorded.
description.sendsNothing: This page sends nothing, so the form was not sent.
description.unknownView: The service sent a view this page does not know ({kind}).
federation.attributePolicyMissing: The assertion verified and the partner is configured, but this realm's attribute policy requires {missing} of every person and the partner supplied no value of it, so nobody was created. Map the attribute on the relationship (fedAttributeMap), or provision the person first.
federation.attributeSourceRefused: {why} This realm's attribute source says a sign-in it cannot read is refused, and the session was ended.
federation.consumerProvidersOff: This relationship is a consumer or social provider, and this realm has federation.consumerProviders off.
federation.disabled: It exists and is configured, and fedEnabled is FALSE. Every relationship is created disabled deliberately: a partner that half-exists and silently accepts assertions is the failure this whole register is arranged to prevent. Enable it on /admin/federation.
federation.fapiNeedsDiscovery: fedFapi is {profile} and fedDiscovery is off. The pushed authorization request endpoint is read from that document, so the sign-in is not started.
federation.formIncomplete: The form was sent {attempts} times without the values this service needs, so nothing was created. Start the sign-in again.
federation.formNoToken: The form did not carry the token this step was given, so nothing was created. Start the sign-in again.
federation.initiateLoginOff: fedInitiateLogin is off on "{id}", so a sign-in its partner starts (OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 4) is refused. Turn it on to accept one; until then a person signs in from this service.
federation.issuerNotPeer: The request names the issuer "{iss}", and this relationship is with "{peer}". OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 4 makes iss REQUIRED, and it is how this service knows which partner started the sign-in.
federation.linkNeedsSignIn: This step needs a sign-in here as {username}, made through the linking screen just now, and this browser holds {held, select, none {none} other {a different one}}. Nothing was linked. Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.linkOtherBrowser: This linking step was started in a different browser, or the cookie that ties it to the one it began in is gone. Nothing was linked. Start the federated sign-in again, in one browser.
federation.linkSignInEnded: Linking your account at the partner to {username} needs you to sign in here as {username} first, and that sign-in ended without one ({asked}). Nothing was linked and nothing was written.
federation.linkSubjectChanged: While you were signing in, the partner's subject came to name {named} rather than {username}. Nothing was linked. Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.linkSubjectChangedSomebody: While you were signing in, the partner's subject came to name somebody else rather than {username}. Nothing was linked. Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.noAccountCreated: The assertion verified, and this service will not create an account from it.
federation.noEntryAutocreateOff: The assertion verified and the partner is configured, but this service holds no directory entry for {username}, and dynamic provisioning (fedAutocreateUsers) is off on this relationship, so the person has to be created here first — through SCIM, /admin/users/new or the management API — and linked to the partner's subject.
federation.noEntryNotCreated: The assertion verified and the partner is configured, but this service holds no directory entry for {username}, and the directory would not create one (the subject policy refused it, the relationship's fedProvisionCap is full, or the directory is full).
federation.noIssuer: The request names no issuer, and this relationship is with "{peer}". OpenID Connect Core 1.0 section 4 makes iss REQUIRED, and it is how this service knows which partner started the sign-in.
federation.noLinkWaiting: The linking step "{handle}" is not one this service started, it has already been used, or it expired (federation.requestTtlMin). Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.noParEndpoint: fedFapi is {profile} and the discovery document names no pushed_authorization_request_endpoint.
federation.noRelationship: There is no relationship called {id}. The configured ones are on the federation index.
federation.noSessionStarted: The assertion verified, and this service will not start a session from it.
federation.noStep: The step "{handle}" is not one this service started, it has already been used, or it expired (federation.requestTtlMin). Start the sign-in again.
federation.noStepFederated: The step "{handle}" is not one this service started, it has already been used, or it expired (federation.requestTtlMin). Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.notAnIdentifier: Type an address such as user@example.com, or a URL.
federation.notConfigured: It is enabled, but {missing} {count, plural, one {is} other {are}} still empty. It refuses rather than half-working — a federated sign-in that got half way and produced a session would be the worst possible outcome.
federation.notFoundByWebFinger: fedWebFinger and fedDiscovery must both be on, and the relationship enabled and fully configured, before an identifier is looked up for it.
federation.off: federation.enabled is off, so no federation endpoint answers. No relationship was changed.
federation.otherWay: "{id}" is an identity-provider-side relationship: this service ASSERTS to that partner rather than consuming from it. There is nothing to sign in to here. A partner this service both consumes from and asserts to is two relationships — see federation/CLAUDE.md.
federation.policyRefusedSession: The assertion verified and the partner is configured — this service will not start a session for {username} because the issuance policy said no. That is a POLICY decision rather than a problem with the assertion or with the partner, so retrying will not change it. The role an application requires is on /admin/roles and the document that decides is on /admin/xacml.
federation.providerNotThisPartner: WebFinger named the issuer "{issuer}", which does not begin with this relationship's fedPeer "{peer}". Only an issuer within the partner an administrator configured is used.
federation.recordedOnAfter: , and every refusal is also a row in the audit log.
federation.recordedOnBefore: This is recorded on the relationship as fedLastError. The whole record is at
federation.refusesHere: This service refuses rather than accepting here, which is the opposite of what it does everywhere else. What arrives at a federation endpoint is an unauthenticated request claiming to be a person, and the session it would produce is the one every other protocol in this process reads. See federation/CLAUDE.md.
federation.relationshipGonePartner: The relationship "{id}" is disabled, half-configured or gone since the partner answered.
federation.relationshipGoneProvider: The relationship "{id}" is disabled, half-configured or gone since the provider answered.
federation.requestNotMade: The request could not be made.
federation.sendsNothing: This page sends nothing, so the form was not sent.
federation.ssfSignsNobodyIn: "{id}" is an ssf relationship: the partner sends this service Shared Signals, and signs nobody in.
federation.stepOtherBrowser: This step was started in a different browser, or the cookie that ties it to the one it began in is gone. Start the sign-in again, in one browser.
federation.stepOtherBrowserFederated: This step was started in a different browser, or the cookie that ties it to the one it began in is gone. Start the federated sign-in again, in one browser.
federation.stepUpNeedsFactor: This sign-in needed a second factor held here, as {username}, made just now, and this browser holds {held, select, none {none} other {a different authentication}}. Start the federated sign-in again.
federation.unknownView: The service sent a view this page does not know ({kind}).
federation.webFingerNoIssuer: WebFinger at {host} named no OpenID Connect issuer.
federation.what.attributeSourceRefused: An attribute source refused the sign-in
federation.what.failedLookingUp: This service failed while looking the identifier up
federation.what.failedStarting: This service failed while starting the sign-in
federation.what.fapiNeedsDiscovery: This FAPI profile needs the partner's discovery document
federation.what.fapiNotSigned: The FAPI request could not be signed
federation.what.mayNotStart: That partner may not start a sign-in here
federation.what.noParEndpoint: The partner publishes no pushed authorization request endpoint
federation.what.noProviderFound: No OpenID Provider was found for that identifier
federation.what.notAnIdentifier: That is not an identifier WebFinger can look up
federation.what.notConfigured: That relationship is not fully configured
federation.what.notFoundByWebFinger: That partner is not found by WebFinger here
federation.what.notProvisioned: This person has not been provisioned
federation.what.notRegistered: This service could not register at the OpenID Provider
federation.what.opConfigurationUnusable: The OpenID Provider's configuration could not be used
federation.what.opNotTrusted: The OpenID Provider could not be trusted
federation.what.otherWay: That relationship goes the other way
federation.what.policyRefusedSession: The issuance policy refused the session
federation.what.providerNotThisPartner: That OpenID Provider is not this partner
federation.what.requestObjectNotSigned: The Request Object could not be signed
gnap.alreadyAnswered: An answer to this request has already been recorded — on this page in another tab, or by a second submission of it. It is answered once.
gnap.answerNotCompleted: The answer could not be completed.
gnap.codeNotRecognised: That code is not recognised, or it has expired.
gnap.csrfStale: The {header} header is missing or is not this browser's. Load the page again.
gnap.heading.alreadyAnswered: This request has already been answered
gnap.heading.linkUsed: This link has already been used
gnap.heading.notWaiting: This request is not waiting for you
gnap.jsonBody: This operation takes a JSON body (Content-Type: application/json).
gnap.limitControlBad: A limit control is not one this page draws, or carries more than a limit can: {names}.
gnap.limitsNotAccepted: These limits could not be accepted: {why}
gnap.linkNotActive: The link does not belong to a request that is still waiting for approval — it may have expired, been used already, or been answered.
gnap.linkOnce: Each interaction link works once (RFC 9635 section 4).
gnap.noSession: This browser holds no session for this page. Load the page again.
gnap.notWaiting: There is no request waiting for approval at this address, or it was already answered or has expired.
gnap.notYours: It asks for access to a resource that is not yours to give: {why} Only its owner can approve it.
gnap.nothingApproved: Nothing was approved and nothing was sent to any application. Start again from the application that sent you here.
gnap.off: This trust realm does not run GNAP (gnap.enabled).
gnap.requestNotCompleted: The request could not be completed.
gnap.tooManyCodes: Too many codes have been tried from here. {detail}
gnap.wrongOrigin: This operation is sent by a page of this service: the request carried {carried, select, none {no Origin} other {another origin}}.
logout.accountNotSignedIn: That account is not signed in in this browser any more. Choose again.
logout.accountsOff: This trust realm does not keep several signed-in accounts per browser (authn.multipleAccounts is off), so there is no account to choose.
logout.chooseAccount: Choose an account, or every account.
logout.familyUnreadable: This could not be read: {failure}. Everything else on this page is unaffected, and a global logout still tries this family again.
logout.nameRefusedAnyUserOff: logout.anyUser is off on this instance, so /logout acts only on the session you are holding. It was asked about "{asked}". To sign another person out, use /admin/logout (the console's Admin Write role) or POST /admin-api/logout (an access token carrying admin:write).
logout.nameRefusedProduct: This service is in product mode, where a sign-out cannot name somebody else whatever logout.anyUser says, so /logout acts only on the session you are holding. It was asked about "{asked}". To sign another person out, use /admin/logout (the console's Admin Write role) or POST /admin-api/logout (an access token carrying admin:write).
logout.noSessionClosed: There is no session cookie on this request, and naming somebody is closed ({closed, select, anyUser {logout.anyUser is off} other {product mode}}), so there is nobody for this endpoint to act on. Sign in at /authn/login first.
logout.noSessionOpen: There is no session cookie on this request. Name somebody with ?username=, or sign in at /authn/login first.
logout.nobodyToSignOutClosed: There is nobody to sign out: this request carries no session cookie, and naming somebody is closed ({closed, select, anyUser {logout.anyUser is off} other {product mode}}).
logout.nobodyToSignOutOpen: There is nobody to sign out: this request carries no session cookie and named no username. A POST is never redirected to the sign-in screen — a 303 would make it a GET and the fields would be gone.
logout.nothingTicked: Nothing is ticked, so nothing was ended.
logout.refusedDevelopment: Sign in as that person at /authn/login — no password is checked in development mode /admin/logout is the operator's door and is behind the console's two roles.
logout.refusedVerifies: Signing yourself out needs no role; signing somebody else out is an act on their account and needs the operator's door. /admin/logout is the operator's door and is behind the console's two roles.
logout.row.claimsTokenEnded: that persisted claims token had already ended
logout.row.codeRedeemed: that authorization code has already been redeemed or has expired, so there is nothing left to end
logout.row.credentialForgotten: that credential is no longer in the issued register — it has been forgotten to the cap since this list was drawn, at which point this service has no position on it left to state
logout.row.gnapGrantFinalized: that GNAP grant had already been finalized
logout.row.gnapGrantGone: that GNAP grant has already been revoked or finalized
logout.row.grantGone: that grant has already been revoked or has expired
logout.row.grantRevoked: that grant has already been revoked
logout.row.noSession: there was no session {handle} to end; it had already expired or already been signed out
logout.row.partnerHsm: the partner cannot be told: its sign-out is signed by a key in the HSM, and it was not signed ahead of this sign-out
logout.row.partnerSessionEnded: the session that partner signed in has already ended
logout.row.preAuthorizedRedeemed: that pre-authorized code has already been redeemed or has expired, so there is nothing left to end
logout.row.realmSessionEnded: the session that realm was signed into on has already ended, which took its cleanup list with it
logout.row.rpSessionEnded: the session that relying party was signed into on has already ended, which signed it out too
logout.row.spSessionEnded: the session that service provider was signed into on has already ended, which took its logout list with it
logout.row.walletCredentialDisowned: that wallet credential has already been disowned or has expired
logout.row.walletSignInCollected: that wallet sign-in has already been collected or has expired, so there is nothing left to end
logout.signInAgain: Sign in again, then come back to end your other sessions.
logout.unreachable: The service could not be reached, so nothing was signed out. Check the connection and try again.
spnego.off: This service can sign people in with a Kerberos ticket, and {setting} is set to false.
spnego.sendsNothing: This page sends nothing, so the form was not sent.
wallet.alreadyUsed: This sign-in has already been used.
wallet.anotherIssuer: The credential verified against a certificate in oid4vp.trustedIssuerCertificates, not against this realm's own key. A credential another issuer signed may be presented to this Verifier, and it does not sign anybody in here: only a credential this realm issued can say who a person here is.
wallet.answerWrongOrigin: A wallet's answer is accepted only from the page on {origin} that asked for it.
wallet.cannotSignRequest: This service cannot sign a wallet request at the moment ({reason}). Sign in another way.
wallet.credentialMismatch: The credential does not match what this realm recorded when it issued it (its subject or the key it is bound to), so it signs nobody in.
wallet.dcApiEmpty: Nothing came back from the browser's Digital Credentials API. Use the same-device link instead.
wallet.declined: The wallet declined to present a credential ({error}), so nobody was signed in.
wallet.didActNeedsEnrolment: A DID act is an enrolment's, started from the portal of the person signed in here.
wallet.didRealmKey: The self-issued ID Token names {subject}, a DID this realm published with a key it keeps, which signs nobody in.
wallet.didUnproved: The self-issued ID Token names {subject}, a DID this realm published with a key it handed over and nobody has proved with a wallet; prove it on your portal's Self-issued IDs page first.
wallet.disownedReinstate: This credential has been disowned: {reason}. It still verifies, and it signs nobody in here any more — its status list says so too. An administrator of this service may reinstate it.
wallet.disownedReissue: This credential has been disowned: {reason}. It still verifies, and it signs nobody in here any more — its status list says so too. A credential issued to you after that will: get one issued again on the Wallet page of your account.
wallet.enrolNeedsSession: A self-issued key is enrolled for the person who is signed in, from their own portal, and this browser holds no sign-on session.
wallet.enrolSignedOut: You are no longer signed in as the person this enrolment was for.
wallet.entryGone: The directory entry this credential was issued for no longer exists — it was deleted, or its name now belongs to a different entry — so the credential signs nobody in.
wallet.heading.alreadyUsed: This sign-in has already been used
wallet.heading.answerNotFromPage: That answer did not come from this page
wallet.heading.cannotMakeRequest: A wallet request could not be made
wallet.heading.didActNotStarted: That DID act cannot be started
wallet.heading.nothingWaiting: Nothing is waiting for this sign-in
wallet.heading.otherBrowser: This sign-in was started in another browser
wallet.heading.policyRefused: The issuance policy refused this sign-in
wallet.heading.responseCodeNotThis: That response code is not this sign-in's
wallet.heading.signInBeforeEnrolling: Sign in before enrolling a wallet
wallet.heading.signInOff: Signing in with a wallet is off
wallet.heading.walletNotRegistered: That wallet address is not registered
wallet.idTokenNotVerified: The self-issued ID Token did not verify, so it signs nobody in. The checks above say which rule it broke.
wallet.keyForSeveralPeople: This wallet key was issued credentials for more than one person here, and an ldp_vc presentation does not say which credential it came from, so it signs nobody in.
wallet.mdocKeyMismatch: The mdoc does not match the device key this realm recorded when it issued it, so it signs nobody in.
wallet.neverStarted: This sign-in was never started here, or it has expired. Each lives oid4vp.signInTtlS seconds.
wallet.notCompleted: The sign-in could not be completed.
wallet.notFinishedTryShortly: This sign-in could not be finished just now; try again shortly.
wallet.notIssuedHere: This realm has no record of issuing this credential to a person it authenticated. Only a credential this realm's issuer minted on an access token this realm issued and verified — for a person, for credential issuance, and not disowned since — may sign somebody in. A credential from another realm, one issued on a token this service did not issue, or one issued before a restart in development mode is not one.
wallet.notOneHolder: The self-issued ID Token and the presentation did not both verify for one holder, so nobody was signed in.
wallet.nothingWaiting: A wallet sign-in continues a request that is waiting at the sign-in screen, and this link names none — it was never started, it has expired, or it has been used.
wallet.otherBrowser: A wallet sign-in finishes only in the browser that started it. If that was you, go back to that browser; otherwise somebody sent you a link to their own sign-in.
wallet.policyRefusedVerified: Your presentation verified. This service will not start a session for this identity. That is a policy decision rather than anything wrong with the credential.
wallet.presentationNotVerified: The presentation did not verify, so it signs nobody in. The checks above say which rule it broke.
wallet.requestExpired: The request you were signing in for has expired. Start again from the application.
wallet.responseCodeMismatch: The link your wallet sent you back with does not carry the code this service gave it.
wallet.selfIssuedNotSecondFactor: A self-issued ID is not offered as a second factor.
wallet.signInOff: This service can sign people in with a verifiable presentation, and oid4vp.signIn is set to false. Turn it on at /admin/oid4vp, or with POST /admin-api/config/set. The Verifier still checks the presentations a verification asks for (POST /admin-api/verifications/start); it signs nobody in.
wallet.statusNotGood: The credential's status says it is no longer good ({detail}), so it signs nobody in.
wallet.statusRevokedOrSuspended: The credential's status says it is no longer good (revoked or suspended), so it signs nobody in.
wallet.subjectNotEnrolled: The self-issued ID Token verified, and its subject {subject} is not enrolled for anybody here. A self-issued key signs in only the person who enrolled it — sign in another way and enrol it on your portal's Self-issued IDs page.
wallet.verdict.selfIssuedNotVerified: The self-issued ID Token did not verify.
web.answeredNoJson: The service answered {status} with no JSON.
web.noOperation: This control has no API operation ({control}), so the page refuses it rather than guess.
web.noState: The service sent no state for it.
web.noStepToRestart: This page names no sign-in step to start over from.
web.notDrawnTitle: This page could not be drawn
web.unreachable: The service's API could not be reached.
